capitals.name: Elbistan
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Elbistan (1337-1507); Marash (1507-1522)'. Coordinates are the town's; Elbistan is not in the gazetteer's places.

correction.text: the region of Elbistan; the 1344 outline is the nearest available shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1337-1343, before Cliopatria's row: Zayn al-Din Qaraja 'established himself in the region of Elbistan in 1335, taking the town in 1337'. The page names no other town, so the 1344 outline is used. Unverified beyond Elbistan.

30,295 km2 for 1344-1374: Elbistan, Maras, Adiyaman and part of Malatya (gazetteer: 37 of 53 cells of K. Maras province, 30 of 44 of Malatya, 20 of 26 of Adiyaman). The infobox gives 70,000 km2 without a year, a ratio of 0.43 to the shape, beyond a factor of two; the pages list no towns beyond Elbistan and Marash, so I cannot say which is wrong. The infobox figure is undated and may be the peak extent or the later sanjak; the shape stands as the early outline. Malatya lies inside this shape (checked on the gazetteer), but the Mamluk Sultanate page has 'a revolt in Syria in 1389 by the Mamluk governors of Malatya and Aleppo', and the war page calls it 'the Mamluk city of Malatya' in the 1480s; Cliopatria's Mamluk shape of 1480 contains none of it.
30,246 km2 for 1375-1384, 49 km2 smaller than 1344: a boundary adjustment; the page is silent. Cliopatria's Mamluk row becomes a neighbour in 1375.

correction.text: the 1385 shape without Malatya and its district, held by a Mamluk governor in 1389

keyframe_review.note: 30,319 km2 for 1385-1401, 73 km2 more than 1375 (the Ramadanid Emirate appears as a neighbour in 1385). The Mamluk page puts Malatya under a Mamluk governor in 1389, yet the shape contains it. Malatya and its district are removed; the Mamluk dossier should carry the matching land. The radius is my reading of 'Malatya'.

30,831 km2 for 1402-1406, 512 km2 more than 1385 (the Timurid Empire is a neighbour 1402-1406): a boundary change the page does not describe. The Dulkadir page is silent on Bayezid I's and Timur's dealings with it. Malatya lies inside this shape (checked on the gazetteer), but the Mamluk Sultanate page has 'a revolt in Syria in 1389 by the Mamluk governors of Malatya and Aleppo', and the war page calls it 'the Mamluk city of Malatya' in the 1480s; Cliopatria's Mamluk shape of 1480 contains none of it.
30,414 km2 for 1407-1439 (Aq Qoyunlu a neighbour from 1407); boundary adjustment, page silent. Malatya's status in these years is not on the pages opened.
30,368 km2 for 1440-1462, 46 km2 less than 1407; boundary adjustment, page silent.

correction.text: the 1463 shape without Malatya and its district, 'the Mamluk city of Malatya'

keyframe_review.note: 30,414 km2 for 1463-1511. The war page has Bozkurt attack 'the Mamluk city of Malatya' at the start of the war of 1485 and says the 1491 treaty left the boundaries 'essentially unchanged'; the Mamluk page has Shah Suwar 'defeated in 1471 by a Mamluk expedition'. The shape contains Malatya; it is removed here (the radius is my reading), and the Mamluk dossier should carry it. Whether Malatya was Mamluk in 1463-1484 is not on the pages opened.

correction.text: the 1512 shape without Malatya and its district, valid to June 1515

keyframe_review.note: 30,414 km2 for 1512-1515, identical to 1463; the beylik ends on 13 June 1515 at Turnadag ('Both Bozkurt and his sons were killed in the battle. After the battle, Beylik of Dulkadir ceased to exist'); the Safavids, listed as a neighbour from 1512, are not mentioned by the page. Malatya as for 1463.

ledger.note: 1337: Zayn al-Din Qaraja takes Elbistan and founds the Dulkadir beylik. He 'established himself in the region of Elbistan in 1335, taking the town in 1337' (infobox 'Established: 1337'); he obtained the title of na'ib from the Mamluk sultan al-Nasir Muhammad.

1485: Bozkurt attacks Malatya, opening the Ottoman-Mamluk war for Dulkadir. 'The war began when Bozkurt attacked the Mamluk city of Malatya' with Bayezid's support; the page gives no year for the attack, so the war's opening year is used.

May 1491: peace ends the Ottoman-Mamluk war. 'a peace treaty was eventually sealed in May 1491'; the boundaries 'remained essentially unchanged'. The treaty is not described as naming Dulkadir or Malatya.
1507: the seat moves from Elbistan to Marash (infobox 'Elbistan (1337-1507); Marash (1507-1522)').

13 June 1515: Selim I destroys Dulkadir at Turnadag. 'In 1515, after the Battle of Turnadag, the principality was conquered by the Ottoman Sultan Selim I'; 'Both Bozkurt and his sons were killed in the battle'; early fighting 13 June 1515 near Goksun.

13 June 1515: the Dulkadir beylik ends. 'After the battle, Beylik of Dulkadir ceased to exist'; the first governor of the sanjak was Ali Bey of the Dulkadir. The infobox gives 1522 and the Dulkadir Eyalet page says the Dulkadirids 'stayed independent until 1521'.

wars.name: Mamluk expedition against Shah Suwar
wars.outcome: 'Shah Suwar was defeated in 1471 by a Mamluk expedition led by Qaitbay's top field commander, Yashbak min Mahdi'; Shah Suwar was the Dulkadirid ruler the Ottomans backed.
wars.note: The Mamluk dossier records the Dulkadirids as Mamluk vassals from 1471.

wars.name: Ottoman-Mamluk War (1485-1491)
wars.outcome: Bozkurt's attack on Malatya opened the war; Dulkadir forces supported the Ottoman army in 1487 and the Dulkadirids appear on both sides after 1488; peace in May 1491 left the boundaries essentially unchanged.
wars.note: The page does not describe Dulkadir as a Mamluk vassal: its Turkmen buffer principalities 'regularly switched their allegiance from one power to the other'. Fighting at Adana (9 February 1486, 26 August 1488) lay outside Dulkadir.

wars.name: Battle of Turnadag
wars.outcome: The Ottomans under Selim I defeated Bozkurt on 13 June 1515 near Goksun; Bozkurt and his sons were killed and the beylik became an Ottoman sanjak.
wars.note: The page calls Dulkadir 'a semi-independent Anatolian beylik under the sovereignty of Mamluk Egypt' and adds that 'The next year, Selim I waged a war against Egypt'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line except the 1491 Ottoman-Mamluk treaty, which left the boundaries 'essentially unchanged' without describing them; the Taurus and Anti-Taurus frontiers are approximate.

notes: Pages: five (budget 5). The Dulkadir page is thin: it gives the founding (1335, 1337), capitals, Selim I's conquest in 1515 and an undated 70,000 km2, but no Mamluk, Karamanid, Ramadanid or Timurid episode; the Mamluk Sultanate page gives only 1471 and c. 1483-1484 for Dulkadir; the war page gives Dulkadir no year. End: 13 June 1515 (Turnadag page) against the infobox's 1522 and the Dulkadir Eyalet page's 'independent until 1521'. Area: shapes of 30,246-30,831 km2 against the infobox 70,000 km2 (ratio 0.43): unresolved, pages list no towns; the shape is kept except for Malatya. Malatya: the shape contains it in every year, the Mamluk page shows a Mamluk governor there in 1389 and the war page a Mamluk city in the 1480s, and Cliopatria's Mamluk shape of 1480 lacks it (0 of 19 cells at 40 km; the Ottoman shape holds 3): shapes 1385, 1463 and 1512 are corrected to exclude Malatya and its district (radius is my reading), so the Mamluk dossier (mamluk-sultanate, me-09) must carry the land or it is nobody's. Vassalage: the mamluk-sultanate dossier's ledger records Dulkadir as a Mamluk vassal from 1471; the pages here only say 'obtaining the title of na'ib' (undated) and 'semi-independent ... under the sovereignty of Mamluk Egypt' in 1515, so no vassal events are recorded here (they belong to the suzerain's dossier). Shape changes of 1375, 1385, 1402, 1407, 1440 are under 2 percent each and unexplained by the pages. Gazetteer name needed: place 'Elbistan' (Kahramanmaras province, lon 37.19, lat 38.21). No ruler list was extracted (Bozkurt 1480-1515 and Ali Beg 1515-1522 only), so identity.rulers is omitted. The Dulkadir page's infobox also lists the Mamluk Sultanate as a predecessor.
